title: Identification of two robust subclasses of sepsis with both prognostic and therapeutic values based on machine learning analysis
summary: Two transcriptomic subtypes were identified in 1,692 sepsis samples; cluster B had higher observed mortality in the cohort with survival data (60.7% vs 39.3%; p=.044). In a separate dataset, risk scores were associated with response to early supportive therapy (p=.027; AUC .663, 95% CI .516-.789). The two-cluster structure and expression/pathway patterns were assessed in five independent datasets (617 samples). The seven-gene prognostic score used separate training (980) and validation (760) sets. Therapy-response association was assessed in GSE110487 only and is modest/retrospective; it does not establish a treatment effect. The therapy-response association is retrospective and does not establish treatment efficacy or causality.
ai_technology: K-means clustering of transcriptomic profiles defined the two sepsis subtypes; LASSO and logistic regression produced the seven-gene risk score linked to clinical outcomes.
